issues.failure_explanation: In the proof of Lemma 3.1, the author bounds the diagonal and off-diagonal entries of $a_h^E$ separately by $c_*$ and $c^*$ and asserts that $\varepsilon_4$ can be chosen satisfying $\frac{c^*}{\gamma c_*} < \varepsilon_4 < \frac{c_*}{c^*}$. This requires $\frac{1}{\gamma} < (\frac{c_*}{c^*})^2$. Since $c_* \le 1 \le c^*$, the ratio $(c_*/c^*)^2$ is strictly less than 1. For a general natural material parameter $0 < 1/\gamma < 1$, this condition fails whenever $1/\gamma \ge (c_*/c^*)^2$ (for instance, in the paper's own numerical Setting 1 where $\gamma = 2$, this requires $c_*/c^* > 1/\sqrt{2}$, which does not hold on general polygonal meshes). The analogous claim for $1/\gamma > 1$ would likewise require $\gamma < (c_*/c^*)^2$, which also fails in general.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair:
Avoid separating $a_h^E$ into $a^E$ with constants $c_*$ and $c^*$ prior to completing the square. Because $a_h^E(\cdot, \cdot)$ is itself a symmetric positive definite bilinear form on $\mathcal{W}_{l,E}^h$, the algebraic identity $a_h^E(\varphi_h, \varphi_h) - \frac{2}{\gamma} a_h^E(\psi_h, \varphi_h) + \frac{1}{\gamma} a_h^E(\psi_h, \psi_h) = a_h^E(\varphi_h - \frac{1}{\gamma}\psi_h, \varphi_h - \frac{1}{\gamma}\psi_h) + \frac{1}{\gamma}(1 - \frac{1}{\gamma}) a_h^E(\psi_h, \psi_h)$ holds directly, establishing coercivity on $\|
abla \boldsymbol{\Psi}_h\|_{0}^2$ for any $0 < 1/\gamma < 1$ via $a_h^E(v_h, v_h) \ge c_* a^E(v_h, v_h)$ without any additional restriction on $\gamma$.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of discrete $\mathbb{T}$-coercivity (Lemma 3.1) fails as written for general physical parameters $\gamma$.
issues.title: Invalid parameter choice in proof of discrete T-coercivity
issues.why_classification: The claim of discrete $\mathbb{T}$-coercivity is correct and all downstream results survive intact; the defect is resolved by a routine local algebraic identity using the inner product structure of $a_h^E$.

issues.failure_explanation: The discrete source problem (3.5) defines the right-hand side using $b_h({\bf F}, {\boldsymbol \Psi}_h)$ for general ${\bf F}=(g, f) \in {\bf \mathds{W}} = L^2(\Omega) \times L^2(\Omega)$. By definition, $b_h^E(f, \psi_h)$ contains the stabilization term $S_b^E((I-\Pi_{l,E}^0)f, (I-\Pi_{l,E}^0)\psi_h)$, which depends on the local degrees of freedom $\boldsymbol{\chi}((I-\Pi_{l,E}^0)f)$. These degrees of freedom require evaluating point values at vertices and edge Gauss-Lobatto points, which are undefined for an arbitrary $f \in L^2(\Omega)$. Furthermore, in (3.18) during the proof of Lemma 3.3, the stabilization term $S_b^E$ is asserted to be bounded by $h^{1+r}\|f-\Pi_l^0 f\|_0 \|\hat{\mathbf{G}}\|_{\mathbf{\mathbb{W}}}$, which is mathematically unsupported and false because point-evaluation degrees of freedom cannot be bounded by the $L^2$-norm.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Following standard virtual element methodology, formulate the right-hand side of the discrete source problem without evaluating stabilization on the data, e.g., setting the right-hand side to $(\Pi_l^0 f, \psi_h)_0$ or $(f, \Pi_l^0 \psi_h)_0$. In (3.18), the difference then reduces to $b^E(f - \Pi_l^0 f, z_I - \Pi_l^0 z_I)$ with no $S_b^E$ term, which is bounded directly by $h^{1+r} \|f - \Pi_l^0 f\|_0 \|\hat{\mathbf{G}}\|_{\mathbf{\mathbb{W}}}$ via the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality.
issues.overall_effect: The discrete source problem (3.5) and the discrete solution operator $\mathcal{A}_h$ are ill-defined on $\mathbf{\mathbb{W}}$, and the duality error bound in Lemma 3.3 (and consequently Lemma 3.4 for $\iota = -1$) is invalid as written.
issues.title: Discrete source problem and duality estimate ill-defined for L2 data
issues.why_classification: Adopting the standard VEM formulation for $L^2$ source terms removes the undefined stabilization evaluations without altering any convergence rate, theorem statement, or advertised scope.
